propositions: When a ticket description exceeds the configured cap (verify.max_ticket_description_chars, default 8000) and the plan-review claim gate is enabled, a warning must be displayed at save time (create or edit) on all surfaces (CLI stderr, library logger, MCP result field) stating the actual length, the cap, and that the claim gate will refuse admission until the description is shortened.

The description cap warning is computed after the CREATE/EDIT event is appended so the write always succeeds and is never altered or blocked, and any error in warning generation degrades to None (warning must not affect the write).

The save-time warning uses the same config key and gate-applicability logic (verify.max_ticket_description_chars read by det_floor.py and the new warning, gate enabled checked via _plan_review_gate_applies) that the plan-review guard uses, ensuring single-source consistency.
No warning is emitted when the gate is disabled, when the description is within the cap, or when the ticket type is plan-review exempt (e.g., bug).

CLI channel outputs 'Warning: …' to stderr with stdout remaining pure in both text and json modes and exit code 0; library surface returns the warning from edit_ticket and includes it in create_ticket(return_alias=True); MCP returns it as an optional description_warning field on CreateResultOut and WriteAckOut.
